candidate.blueprint_locator: Management of Care activity statements, printed p. 7: participate in performance/quality improvement, manage conflict, utilize resources for quality care; Appendix A Management concepts/collaboration as applicable.
candidate.blueprint_topic: Management of Care — systems improvement, staff support, and care-delivery operations
candidate.educational_objective: Address healthcare-worker burnout with a systems approach that engages staff and targets modifiable operational drivers rather than relying primarily on individual resilience interventions.

options.A: Offer resilience training while leaving staffing, scheduling, workload, and administrative processes unchanged.
options.B: Focus primarily on individual coping and avoid reviewing work-system causes because operational changes may be disruptive.
options.C: Engage staff in reviewing modifiable work-system drivers and pursue operational improvements in areas such as staffing, scheduling, workload, administrative burden, safety, and support.
options.D: Increase mandatory overtime to fill staffing gaps while expanding mindfulness and other individual wellness resources.

candidate.rationale: NIOSH's Impact Wellbeing Guide explicitly uses a systems approach and instructs leaders to go beyond encouraging self-care and individual resilience by focusing on operational-level improvements. NIOSH campaign findings identify systemic drivers such as inadequate staffing, demanding or unpredictable schedules, and excessive administrative work, and emphasize staff involvement and two-way communication. Therefore, reviewing and changing modifiable work conditions with staff best reflects the approach; individual wellness resources may complement but should not substitute for system-level improvements.
candidate.source_claim_supported: NIOSH directs leaders to go beyond individual resilience toward operational improvements, review hospital operations, involve staff through two-way communication, and address systemic burnout drivers including staffing, demanding schedules, and excessive administrative work.
candidate.source_locator: Impact Wellbeing Guide → 'Key principles' (Use a systems approach; Build trust) and Action 1 'Review Your Hospital's Operations'; Campaign Insights → systemic factors at the root of staff burnout.
candidate.source_organization: CDC, National Institute for Occupational Safety and Health (NIOSH)
candidate.source_version_date: Impact Wellbeing Guide page 2024-09-16; NIOSH Publication 2024-109 revised 2024-07
candidate.stem: A nurse manager identifies rising burnout, short staffing, unpredictable schedules, and excessive administrative burden on the unit. Which response best reflects NIOSH's systems approach to healthcare-worker wellbeing?
